question: Clutch time means the last 5 minutes of the 4th quarter or any overtime, when the score is within 5 points. Which team had the best clutch net points (points scored minus points allowed during clutch plays) in the 2022-23 regular season?
answer:
In the 2022-23 NBA regular season, the **Miami Heat (MIA)** had the best clutch net points, outscoring their opponents by **+70** during clutch plays. 

*Clutch time is defined as the 4th quarter or overtime, with 5:00 or less remaining, when the score margin is within 5 points going into the play.*

### Top 10 Teams by Clutch Net Points (2022-23 Regular Season)

| Team | Clutch Games | Clutch Points For | Clutch Points Against | Clutch Net Points | Clutch Record | Clutch Win % |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Miami Heat (MIA)** | 49 | 479 | 409 | **+70** | 30-19 | 61.2% |
| **Philadelphia 76ers (PHI)** | 40 | 372 | 312 | **+60** | 24-16 | 60.0% |
| **New Orleans Pelicans (NOP)** | 32 | 337 | 282 | **+55** | 17-15 | 53.1% |
| **Sacramento Kings (SAC)** | 42 | 497 | 449 | **+48** | 24-18 | 57.1% |
| **Los Angeles Lakers (LAL)** | 40 | 377 | 335 | **+42** | 21-19 | 52.5% |
| **Denver Nuggets (DEN)** | 36 | 324 | 285 | **+39** | 21-15 | 58.3% |
| **Milwaukee Bucks (MIL)** | 32 | 283 | 245 | **+38** | 25-7 | 78.1% |
| **Cleveland Cavaliers (CLE)** | 41 | 355 | 320 | **+35** | 22-19 | 53.7% |
| **Minnesota Timberwolves (MIN)** | 42 | 339 | 309 | **+30** | 25-17 | 59.5% |
| **Utah Jazz (UTA)** | 52 | 489 | 468 | **+21** | 23-29 | 44.2% |

### Key Caveats & Observations

* **Volume vs. Efficiency:** The Miami Heat played a massive number of clutch games (49), which gave them more opportunities to accumulate a high total point differential. On a per-game basis, the New Orleans Pelicans (+1.72 net points per clutch game) and the Philadelphia 76ers (+1.50) were slightly more dominant than Miami (+1.43) when they were actually playing in clutch situations.
* **Point Differential vs. Winning Record:** Total net points in clutch time do not perfectly map to clutch win-loss records. For instance, the Milwaukee Bucks only had a +38 clutch point differential across 32 games, but they managed a spectacular 25-7 (78.1%) record in those games by consistently grinding out narrow victories. 
* **Fluid Clutch Window:** Because clutch status is evaluated on a play-by-play basis, games frequently slip in and out of the clutch window. If a team hit a late shot to push a 5-point lead to 7 points, subsequent plays in that game were no longer counted as "clutch plays" unless the opponent trimmed the deficit back down.

args.query:
SELECT team, COUNT(*) AS clutch_games, SUM(clutch_pts_for) AS pts_for, SUM(clutch_pts_against) AS pts_against,
       SUM(clutch_pts_for - clutch_pts_against) AS net_pts,
       ROUND(AVG(clutch_pts_for - clutch_pts_against), 2) AS net_per_game
FROM team_game_clutch
WHERE season_start_year = 2022 AND season_type = 'Regular Season'
GROUP BY team
ORDER BY net_pts DESC

SELECT t.team, COUNT(*) AS clutch_games,
       SUM((g.winner = t.team)::INT) AS wins,
       COUNT(*) - SUM((g.winner = t.team)::INT) AS losses,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM((g.winner = t.team)::INT) / COUNT(*), 1) AS win_pct
FROM team_game_clutch t JOIN games g USING (game_id)
WHERE t.season_start_year = 2022 AND t.season_type = 'Regular Season'
GROUP BY t.team
ORDER BY SUM(clutch_pts_for - clutch_pts_against) DESC
LIMIT 10
